chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever eats clay and dies, he has aided in his own death.'

key_terms.أَعَانَ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ: Aided in his own death / Self-inflicted death

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating clay and dying from it?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration linking the consumption of clay (*al-tilaa'*) to self-inflicted death, a concept often discussed in the context of *al-ghasab* (usurption) of one's own life. This ruling carries practical implications for inheritance distribution and burial rites, distinguishing it from natural causes of death. The hadith underscores the physical and spiritual harm of consuming earth, a practice prevalent in pre-Islamic and early Islamic Arabia.
